exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ runs callables concurrently in a pool of OS threads and is commonly useful for overlapping blocking I/O.

reveal.text: ThreadPoolExecutor runs callables concurrently in a pool of OS threads and is commonly useful for overlapping blocking I/O.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ ThreadPoolExecutor() as pool: futures = [pool.submit(fetch, url) for url in urls] submits independent calls.

reveal.text: with ThreadPoolExecutor() as pool: futures = [pool.submit(fetch, url) for url in urls] submits independent calls.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ do not normally provide multi-core speedups for CPU-bound pure Python because of the regular CPython GIL.

reveal.text: Threads do not normally provide multi-core speedups for CPU-bound pure Python because of the regular CPython GIL.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ runs work in separate processes, allowing CPU-bound Python code to use multiple cores.

reveal.text: ProcessPoolExecutor runs work in separate processes, allowing CPU-bound Python code to use multiple cores.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ ProcessPoolExecutor() as pool: results = list(pool.map(score, records)) is a high-level parallel map pattern.

reveal.text: with ProcessPoolExecutor() as pool: results = list(pool.map(score, records)) is a high-level parallel map pattern.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(futures) yields Future objects as each finishes, which is useful when processing results in completion order instead of submission order.

reveal.text: as_completed(futures) yields Future objects as each finishes, which is useful when processing results in completion order instead of submission order.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ future in as_completed(futures): result = future.result() handles fast results without waiting for earlier slow submissions.

reveal.text: for future in as_completed(futures): result = future.result() handles fast results without waiting for earlier slow submissions.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ result() re-raises the worker exception; completion order does not imply submission order.

reveal.text: Calling result() re-raises the worker exception; completion order does not imply submission order.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
